I've been working this land since I was twenty years old. Two mu, wheat then maize, same as my father did. I know this ground.

Wheat goes in around mid-October after I prepare the soil with rotary tillage — that chops up the maize stalks fine. I'll buy improved seed from the county co-op, same variety I've used the last few years, Jimai or similar. I apply base fertilizer when I plant: compound fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium mixed in, plus some urea. Then I top-dress nitrogen at jointing in spring. I water four times — before winter sets in, then jointing, heading, and grain filling. Two pesticide passes: herbicide in winter while weeds are small, then spray for aphids when the heads come out. Expect around 450 jin per mu if the weather holds.

After wheat harvest in June, I turn around and plant maize right away — no-till, straight into the stubble. Saves my back and keeps moisture in. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the seed shop has that everyone else is planting. It doesn't fail me. Base fertilizer goes down at planting, then I chase with urea at jointing. I water three times — at emergence if it's dry, jointing, and grain filling. One herbicide pass early, maybe one more spray if there's corn borer pressure later. Yield should be around 550-600 jin per mu.

Living alone at my age, I keep things simple. I don't experiment. This system works.
